We really enjoyed the food!
Oct 2018 • Couples
We popped in for a quick meal and ordered a dish with stirred fried spaghetti and chicken and a dish with beef w garlic and chili. Both dishes tasted really good, and luckily they served the chicken first as the beef was rather spicy. We paid approximately 350 000 dong for this and four canned Vietnamese beer. So both with regards to taste, service and price this was a very nice experience. The interior/atmosphere etc however was nothing special - more like a college canteen. But a good place for a decent meal.

Most frequented restaurant, 5 to 3 star
Apr 2018 • Friends
I have been frequenting this restaurant and boasting about it for 7 years now. Once an absolute gem, possibly still is however had a bad experience last night with a dish I take regularly (all are do a night with errors).

I eat here because they offer high quality seafoods cooked to order accompanied by a wide range of affordable affair. 

In particular I like the Cá chình nướng (large eel BBQd on real grill) which was brilliantly bbq in the past with bit of salt and chilly (past being years as well as 5 days prior to this reviewed meal). So the entry into the higher priced seafood pushes the price to 1,500,000VND ($65usd) vs 300,000vnd when ordering menu/ non market priced seafood. 

At this price price you except to not be lied to about Bbq vs fry with oil in a pan left dripping wet with oil (now recall o ate this dish here 5 days prior and confirm Bbq (nướng) in Vietnamese. When called out on the shortcut, continually lied about it and said this is an oily fish. 

Seems Din Ky has fallen to the all too familiar lazy lie mentality that is common among tour bait and switch eateries; except this is a high end locals spot. 

Shame on the lazy lie backed by lazy lies and full price bill despite an edible meal (due to fry oil allergy)

Time to retrain staff to not lie and bbq when the most expensive dishes are ordered as Bbq with intent and expressed allergy
